findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

An ordinary final retry sets acknowledgeFailedTurn even when the runner sent no reply or failure notice. handleFailure then keeps the turn's input consumed, so the unanswered message cannot reach a later turn. Release input unless output was delivered.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

Restart recovery releases every follow-up consumed by the failed run, including one the runner received and answered before crashing. The delivered-output check protects only the initial input. The next turn can therefore receive an answered follow-up again; recovery needs to retain follow-ups confirmed as handled.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The subprocess workers only call takeInput and getMessagesByIds, then exit. They never admit a turn or deliver a reply. The active-turn follow-up scenario uses two worker objects in one process, so these tests cannot detect loss or duplication across a real process handoff through reply.
findings.title: Not done: two-process no-loss/no-duplication test

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The supplied Functional check says the covered paths were reviewed and that the focused Postgres command could not run. It does not describe exercising the two-worker, settings-reload, restart, or before- and after-reply failure paths as a user would, leaving material covered behavior out of the required check.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

takeInput selects work items by receiveOrder, but this presentation sort gives provider timestamps precedence. A delayed attachment or a provider timestamp that moves backward can put a later-received message before an earlier one in the agent's batch. Use receiveOrder when available.
findings.title: Present taken messages in receive order

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

This added file records review findings and task status. It is outside the permitted paths and is unnecessary for the runtime switch, migration, tests, or decision update.
findings.title: Remove the review-state file outside the allowed scope

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

On the final retry of an ordinary runner error, `acknowledgeFailedTurn` is true even when no output or failure notice was delivered. `handleFailure` then returns without releasing the consumed input. The next turn cannot take the unanswered message, contrary to the required before-reply failure behavior.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The continuation is marked applied as soon as the host hook writes to runner input. That boolean does not confirm that either runner actually supplied the message to the model. A follow-up accepted near turn completion can therefore remain consumed when the runner exits without reading it, leaving nothing for the next turn to take. The required runner-level delivery confirmation is absent from this path.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The added case calls `app.loadState()` after changing the saved marker. It does not reload runtime settings or exercise the settings reload entry point, so it cannot detect a dropped or duplicated admission item during the required settings reload path.
findings.title: Not done: settings reload
